B8.brief: bench/results/heldout/G9/run-3/B8/brief.md: 'B8 · An emote for the harbourmaster'. A trading game set in an island harbour town: players meet on the quays and pick emotes from a wheel, and the harbourmaster's wheel is one emote short, the one the team wants not being in the m3a library; the studio gives back to the library what it builds from it. It describes the workspace's character as seed 5672 generates it. The job is reworded with every requirement kept: an emote of the agent's choosing for character.glb, made from the CC0 library, sent with npx m3a library submit until it waits in awaiting review with every check green; new to the library (the queue bounces a library clip sent unchanged or barely changed) and not sent with --improves; on the spot (no walking or running as npx m3a describe reads it, under a quarter of its hip height travelled); tagged emote, with a name and a description of its own that say what it does, not its source clip's; complete provenance (method and tool, a CC0 claim, the maker an AI agent named with its Claude model); the local backend in .cache/intake/, checked every 30 s, as the hosted queue is every 15 minutes; npx m3a library status for each submission's state and a bounce's reason, to fix and submit again. The grading paragraph is B8.md's word for word (copied with awk and compared: identical).
B8.character: gen-5672: bulky build, relaxed rest pose (upper arms and forearms 70° below level), VRM 1.0 humanoid names in metres (armature unscaled, no bone node rotated: each bone's frame the world's), facing +z, left on +x, no twist bones, toes left out: hips (the skeleton's root, 1.0138 m above the origin), spine, chest, upperChest, neck, head up the middle; leftShoulder, leftUpperArm, leftLowerArm, leftHand on upperChest; leftUpperLeg, leftLowerLeg, leftFoot on hips; the same with right; 20 bones, one skinned mesh, mesh y -0.042 to 1.835 m (1.88 m tall, hips 1.055 m above its lowest point), x ±0.620 m; a plain GLB with no VRM extension; three.js loads the names unchanged.
B8.how_it_differs: New game and setting (a trading game in an island harbour town, emotes picked from a wheel when players meet on the quays, the harbourmaster its character), a new title and opening, and a description of the character, which B8.md doesn't give. The job's bullets are reworded with every requirement kept; the grading paragraph is B8.md's word for word. No clip, kind of emote or method is named or hinted. The body differs from the brief's own (seed 1: heroic, A, Mixamo, no twist, upperChest left out), from run 1's (seed 9406: heroic, A, UE5, twist, neck left out) and from run 2's (seed 7359: tall, T, Rigify, twist, shoulders left out) in all three of build (bulky), rest pose (relaxed, arms 70° down) and naming (VRM, the one family none of them uses, with world-aligned bone frames), and in the bones left out (toes).

How I picked it: variants.ts maps a seed s to build BUILDS[s%5], rest RESTS[s%3], naming NAMINGS[s%4], twist floor(s/4)%2 === 1, drop DROPS[s%6]. Seeds 1, 9406 and 7359 are heroic/A/Mixamo, heroic/A/UE5 and tall/T/Rigify (variant() confirms), so I took bulky (s%5 = 2), relaxed (s%3 = 2) and VRM (s%4 = 0), new to all three in each: s ≡ 32 mod 60, which fixes the drop as the toes. Every fact about the body in the brief was read off the generated character (character(variant(5672)), its GLB, and the GLB loaded with loadGlb and skeletonIn): the 20 bones with their parents, the hips' head at y 1.0138 m, POSITION's y range -0.0416 to 1.8349 m (the foot tubes' underside to the head tube's top) and x range ±0.6203 m, the upper arms and forearms 70.00° below level on both sides, the foot tubes reaching z +0.2174 (facing +z) and the left bones at +x, the Armature node with no scale, no node with a rotation, 20 skin joints, one skinned mesh, no extensions or extensionsUsed in the GLB (its extras hold only the generator's m3a block), and three.js's names identical to the file's. The brief doesn't state a travel limit in metres, because the grader measures travel on the rest the clip was made on, not on character.glb. I did not run bind or any m3a tool on the body, so the brief claims nothing about how m3a reads the rig. problems.what: The brief gives the hips' height only above the origin: 'its hips joint 1.01 m above the origin'. That is true (y 1.0138). But the hip height m3a measures for the brief's 'a quarter of its hip height' is taken from the ground under the feet. bind's H0 and retarget.inspect both read 1055 mm, and the grader reports 'hips 1055 mm up'. The soles are 0.04 m below the origin. A reader who takes 1.01 m as the hip height sets a slightly stricter limit (0.253 m against 0.264 m), which costs nothing. The brief also gives the mesh's range, from which 1.06 m follows. No stated fact is false.
problems.fix: Optionally, add '(1.06 m above its soles)' after the hips' height.
